subject: READING
prompt: What was the weather like at recess?
passage: It was raining hard at recess. Maya had her big blue umbrella. She noticed a new girl standing alone by the door, getting wet. The girl looked nervous and did not know anyone yet. Maya walked over and held the umbrella over both of them. 'I'm Maya,' she said. 'Want to walk together?' The new girl smiled and said, 'I'm Sofia. Thank you!'
explanation: The first sentence says, 'It was raining hard at recess.'

subject: READING
prompt: What is a group of ants called?
passage: Ants are small, but they are very strong. An ant can carry things that are much heavier than its own body. Ants live together in a group called a colony. Each ant has a job. Some ants dig tunnels. Some ants find food. Other ants take care of the baby ants. The queen ant lays all the eggs. By working together, the ants keep the colony safe and fed.
explanation: The passage says, 'Ants live together in a group called a colony.'

subject: READING
prompt: Where should you put the cup?
passage: You can grow a bean plant at home. First, fill a cup with soil. Next, push a bean seed into the soil with your finger. Then, pour in a little water. Put the cup by a sunny window. Water the seed every few days. In about a week, a tiny green sprout will pop up. Soon it will grow leaves.
explanation: The directions say, 'Put the cup by a sunny window.'

subject: READING
prompt: Which word means almost the same as 'happy'?
explanation: Glad and happy both mean feeling good or pleased.

subject: READING
prompt: Where did Rabbit hide the carrots?
passage: Rabbit found ten carrots in the field. 'These are all mine,' he said. He hid them under a bush and did not tell his friends. That night it rained hard. In the morning, the carrots were soft and rotten. Rabbit was sad. Then Squirrel came by with a basket of nuts. 'Have some of mine,' she said. Rabbit ate the nuts and felt ashamed. The next day he found more carrots. This time he gave some to every friend.
explanation: The story says, 'He hid them under a bush.'

subject: READING
prompt: Read: To make a bird feeder, Jo first tied a string to a pine cone. Next, she spread peanut butter on it. Then she rolled it in seeds. Last, she hung it in a tree. Put the steps in the order Jo did them.
orderedItems: Tie a string to the pine cone
explanation: The words first, next, then, and last show the order: string, peanut butter, seeds, hang in a tree.

subject: READING
prompt: Word bank: loud, tiny, brave. Use each word only once. The ant was so ___ that I needed a magnifying glass to see it. The thunder was so ___ that it woke the baby.
explanation: Something you need a magnifying glass to see is tiny. Thunder that wakes a baby is loud.

subject: READING
prompt: The prefix 're-' means 'again.' Dad had to reheat the soup. What does reheat mean?
explanation: Because 're-' means 'again,' reheat means to heat again.

subject: READING
prompt: Read: Penguins are birds, but they cannot fly. They use their wings to swim fast under the water. Thick feathers keep them warm in the icy cold. Which statements are true according to the text? Select all that apply.
choices: Penguins use their wings to swim
correctAnswers: Penguins use their wings to swim
explanation: The text says penguins 'cannot fly' and 'use their wings to swim.' It says they have thick feathers and live in icy cold, not thin fur or hot deserts.

subject: READING
prompt: Why did Rabbit feel ashamed when he ate the nuts?
passage: Rabbit found ten carrots in the field. 'These are all mine,' he said. He hid them under a bush and did not tell his friends. That night it rained hard. In the morning, the carrots were soft and rotten. Rabbit was sad. Then Squirrel came by with a basket of nuts. 'Have some of mine,' she said. Rabbit ate the nuts and felt ashamed. The next day he found more carrots. This time he gave some to every friend.
choices: He had eaten too many of Squirrel's nuts
Squirrel had found and taken his hidden carrots
He did not like the taste of Squirrel's nuts at all
Squirrel shared with him, but he did not share
correctAnswer: Squirrel shared with him, but he did not share
explanation: Rabbit kept all ten carrots and 'did not tell his friends,' but Squirrel freely said, 'Have some of mine.' Her kindness made him feel bad about not sharing.

subject: READING
prompt: What lesson does Rabbit learn in this story?
passage: Rabbit found ten carrots in the field. 'These are all mine,' he said. He hid them under a bush and did not tell his friends. That night it rained hard. choices: It is good to share with your friends
Carrots must always be kept dry when it rains

Friends should not visit after it rains
